courses.course_name: Contraceptive Management in Reproductive Health for BCCNM Certification
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This 8 week online self-paced, course is for Registered Nurses (RNs) and Registered Midwives (RMs) who are seeking competencies for Contraceptive Management Certified Practice. Students will be provided with the minimum requirements for safe assessment, provision and management of Combined Hormonal Contraception (CHC) and Progestin only Hormonal Contraception. (POHC), including prescribing. It is recommended that learners spend an average of 4 – 6 hours per week of study time. Students will become competent in the certified practice realm of Contraceptive Management (CM) as mandated by the British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives Registered Nurses (BCCNM)). Registered Nurses: Upon completion of the course nurses will write an Exit Evaluation and if successful, will apply to be placed on the BCCNM Certified Practices Register, apply for prescribing authority within their certified practice area and be eligible to use the certified practice designation. Registered Midwives: Upon completion of the course, midwives will write an Exit Evaluation and if successful, will apply to be placed on the BCCNM Specialized Skill Register. BCCNM/NNPBC-approved CM Decision Support Tools (DSTs) are supported by the World Health Organization & US CDC Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use. For full information on BCCNM certified practice please visit www.bccnm.ca/RN/CertifiedPractice/Pages/Default.aspx ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This 12-week online, asynchronous and self-paced course provides students with baseline theoretical knowledge for diagnosing and treating various sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Students will apply the theory learned to the development of clinical skills, within the scope of certified nursing practice, with clients experiencing or at risk for STIs. It is recommended that learners spend an average of 4 – 6 hours per week of study time. Comprehensive assessment integrates history or present illness and review of systems into the sexual history when appropriate. Registered Nurses seeking certification in Reproductive Health – STI Management with the British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) must complete both NSPN 7735 theory course & NSPN 7736 – Sexually Transmitted Infections Management Clinical Course within 6 months in order to be eligible to apply for certified practice designation. Students must be BCCNM registered to be eligible to take the practicum component NSPN 7736. Students who successfully complete both 7735 & 7736, will apply to be placed on the BCCNM Certified Practices Register, apply for prescribing authority within their certified practice area and be eligible to use the certified practice designation. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

admission.raw: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Ongoing throughout the year. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid status in Canada other than study permit. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Apply to program Formal application to the microcredential is not required. Upon successful completion of the courses , email the program contact with your full name, student number, and mailing address to be issued a microcredential. non_course_requirements.raw: Program length This part-time microcredential can be completed in as little as 10 weeks if the courses are taken concurrently. If the courses are taken separately, it will take 16 weeks to complete. Grading All learners must achieve a minimum 75% passing grade, including a 75% on the final exam. Program delivery Online: This program is delivered fully online. Program location Distance and online learning Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs
